NORTH-WEST FRONTIER PROVINCE MUSALIHATI
NORTH-WEST FRONTIER
PROVINCE MUSALIHATI
JARGA (CONSTITUTION
AND FUNCTIONS) RULES, 2006
[Gazette of N.-W.F.P.
Extraordinary,
22nd February, 2006]
No.PO-I(LG)2-443/GJTMA/2004, dated
30-1-2006.---In exercise of the powers conferred under section 191 of the
North-West Frontier Province Local Government Ordinance, 2001, the Government
is pleased to make the following rules, namely:
1. Short title and commencement.---(1)
These rules may be called the North-West Frontier Province Musalihati Jarga
(Constitution and Functions) Rules, 2006.
(2) They shall come into force at once.
2. Definitions.---In these rules, unless
there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,---
(a) "dispute" means quarrel or
disagreement, whether of civil or criminal nature including those specified in
Form I of the Schedule.
(b) "Insaaf Committee" means
Insaaf Committee elected under clause (n) of section 88 of the Ordinance;
(c) "Musalihati Jarga" means a
Musalihati Jarga Constituted under
section 102 of the Ordinance,
read with section
80(d) thereof.
(d) "Musleh" means a member of
the Musalihati Jarga;
(e) "Ordinance" means the
North-West Frontier Province Local Government Ordinance, 2001 (N.-W.F.P. Ord.
No.XIV of 2001);
(f) "Party" means party to a
dispute referred to a Musalihati Jarga;
(g) "Schedule" means a Schedule
appended to these rules;
(h) "Secretary" means the
Secretary of the Union Council concerned; and
(2) Words and expression used but not
defined in these rules shall have the same meanings as assigned to them in the
Ordinance.
Formation of Musalihati
Jarga
3. Constitution of Musalihati Jarga.--(1)
Musalihati Jarga shall be constituted in accordance with subsection (1) of
section 102 of the Ordinance of whom one member may preferably be a woman. The
members of Musalihati Jarga should preferably be able to read and write. The
names of such persons shall be included in the panel after inviting recommendations
from the residents of the Union concerned.
(2) Effort shall be made to have at least
one member of a Musalihati Jarga from amongst persons who have previous legal
experince or have been Headmaster/Principles of a school.
(3) The Union Nazim shall notify the
constitution of the Musalihati Jarga in Form 2 of the Schedule.
(4) The selected Musaleheen shall take
oath before assuming office, which shall be administered by the Union Nazim.
(5) Any casual vacancy in the panel of
Musaleheen shall be filled within two weeks after occurrence thereof, from the
panel maintained by the Insaaf Committee.
(6) Musleh may resign, at any time, in
writing (to the Insaaf Committee) from
the membership of the Musalihati Jarga, but he shall continue to work till his
resignation is accepted by the Insaaf committee.
(7) Where a Musleh (Conciliator) displays
or is accused of partiality or malpractice, an aggrieved person or the Union
Nazim may file a complaint before the Insaaf Committee. If on scrutiny of such
complaint the Insaaf Committee is satisfied that a prima facie case is made
out, it shall summon the complainant and serve notice to show cause to the
accused Musleh listing the grounds rendering him unsuitable for performing his
functions. Upon receipt and consideration of the reply from the accused Musleh
and after hearing the parties, the Insaaf Committee may remove the accused
Musleh and another Musleh shall be selected in his place from the panel
maintained under sub-rule (1).
(8) These rules as well as the names of
the members of the Musalihati Jarga shall be displayed in Urdu and local
language at prominent public places in the Union including the notice board of
the Union Council and the notice board of the Musalihati Jarga.

individual cases.---The parties to a dispute may individually or jointly
